Create an output with N times the input height and N times the input width.
Map each output cell back to its input cell using quotient and to its local block coordinate using modulo.
Fill every block belonging to a nonzero input cell with that input color.
For a zero input cell, inspect NW, NE, SW, SE diagonal neighbours in that exact order.
A diagonal neighbour qualifies only when it is in bounds and nonzero while both intervening orthogonal neighbours are zero.
Use the first qualifying neighbour: NW or SE draws red on the main block diagonal; NE or SW draws red on the anti diagonal.
Leave the rest of every zero block black.

structured_plan_steps: Count colors: choose the modal background, the color appearing exactly twice as the endpoints, the remaining color appearing more than 30 times as the stripe color, and the remaining medium-frequency color as the waypoint color.
Compare the maximum row and column occupancies of stripe cells; transpose the grid when the stripes are vertical so they become horizontal.
In the normalized grid, collect each nearly full stripe row and take the middle column of its contiguous three-cell waypoint run.
Start below the upper endpoint. For each stripe in reading order, draw vertically to the row above it, horizontally to the waypoint center, and one cell through the stripe.
After the last stripe, continue vertically to the lower endpoint row and horizontally to the lower endpoint, preserving all cells not covered by the endpoint-colored path.
Transpose the result back when the input was vertically oriented.

structured_plan_steps: Identify the modal field, the three-column top object, its body and tip colors, and the remaining obstacle color.
Erase the original object cells in rows zero through two.
For each tip-ending column, place two body cells and its tip immediately above the first obstacle, or bottom-aligned when unobstructed.
For each body-only column, normally place three body cells at the bottom edge.
If a body column intersects a bottom-touching obstacle component, choose the nearest tallest component column as its landing column.
For a one-row shelf, clear up to two shelf cells in the side with more room before applying the bottom-aligned body column.

semantic_invariant: The colored object along the top is three rows tall and three columns wide. Treat each of its columns independently. A column whose bottom cell is the tip color falls until that tip is immediately above the first gray obstacle in its column, or rests on the bottom edge if there is no obstacle. A column made entirely of the body color falls to the bottom; when its column meets a bottom-touching gray component, use that component's tallest nearest column as the landing column, clearing the needed cells of a one-row shelf. Preserve all other gray obstacles and erase the object's original top position.

Sort candidates by decreasing number of red cells, breaking equal-count ties by the top-left coordinate in reading order.
Walk that order greedily. Keep a candidate only if none of its red cells belongs to an earlier kept candidate; otherwise skip it.
For each kept candidate, preserve every red cell, recolor its gray center yellow 4, and recolor its other gray cells orange 7.
Leave the dense black/gray noise outside selected windows unchanged.

structured_plan_steps: Mark a column as a gap exactly when both cells in that column are zero, then read the maximal non-gap runs from left to right.
Classify a one-column run as straight. Classify every wider run as left when its upper-left cell is zero and right otherwise.
Initialize the trace state at row 1, column 3.

For straight, paint the current cell and the cell below, then advance two rows. For left or right, paint the two horizontal cells on that side, then advance one row and shift one column in that direction.
Create a fixed 8x7 black grid, paint every traced cell red 2, and put a green 3 marker at row 0, column 3.

Read the runs from left to right: a one-column run means straight down, while a wider run turns left when its upper-left cell is zero and right otherwise. Paint a green 3 at row 0, column 3 and leave every other untraced cell black.

structured_plan_steps: Find connected objects while treating gray (5) as background, yielding the black zero regions separated by gray walls.
For each zero region, compute its top, left, bottom, and right bounding-box coordinates.
Require an in-bounds row of gray cells immediately above the full bounding-box width.
Require an in-bounds row of gray cells immediately below the full bounding-box width.
Require a gray column immediately left of the full bounding-box height, unless the region already touches the left canvas edge.
Require a gray column immediately right of the full bounding-box height, unless the region already touches the right canvas edge.
Reject a region spanning multiple rows when its bounding box is only column zero, even if every wall condition passes.
Paint every cell of each qualifying zero object yellow (4), leaving rejected zero regions and all gray walls unchanged.

semantic_invariant: Treat gray (5) as walls and find each orthogonally connected black zero region. Paint a region yellow (4) only when the complete rows just above and below its bounding box are gray and the complete columns just left and right are gray. The left and right canvas edges count as walls, but the top and bottom edges do not; exclude any multi-row region confined to column zero.
